bus.fromView.anchor: switch(x.type) enclosing case`shared-object-set`: (per-window handleMessage; exhaustive over the union) + ipcMain.handle(<message-from-view const>) front-door `.type===` chain + preamble type-guard delegates (+ `e.type in MAP` delegate handler); quote spelling and chunk of each part are free
bus.fromView.falsePositiveRisk: delegates reached only through a startsWith-guard (avatar-overlay-*) are a prefix family, not enumerated; a new delegate shape is silently missed (see renderer-sent cross-check)

bus.toView.anchor: switch(x.type) enclosing case`persisted-atom-updated`: in the one renderer chunk that has it (the renderer message-for-view dispatcher; exhaustive, no-op cases listed) + preamble type-guard + enum-member labels
bus.toView.falsePositiveRisk: labels that are explicit no-ops (break) are types the renderer receives but handles through another subscriber

bus.fetchHandlers.anchor: none: no main-process file holds the fetch dispatcher ("not implemented in the current Electron process"), the `vscode://codex/` prefix or `handleVSCodeRequest` (the channel is gone; HTTP goes through the AppHost HTTP fetch service)
bus.fetchHandlers.falsePositiveRisk: `retired` means the three strings are absent from every main-process file; a dispatcher rewritten with none of them would read as retired (the renderer still builds vscode://codex/<name> URLs, so check apphost.services for where they went)

ipc.channels.anchor: string literals `codex_desktop:<name>` (colon form) in vite/build files; `${}` segments mark per-worker channels
ipc.channels.falsePositiveRisk: underscore forms (codex_desktop_quic_ssh, ...) are gate/feature names, excluded by the colon; a channel built by concatenation would be missed

state.globalKeys.anchor: object literal containing LOCAL_PROJECTS:<"local-projects"> (enum NAME:"value", any quote); one copy per bundled file: the app-shared chunk and a display worker chunk in the renderer, the shared lib (and, before 22943, the worker bundle) in the main process
state.globalKeys.falsePositiveRisk: enum members whose value is not a plain string literal would be skipped (none)

state.persistedAtoms.anchor: one rspack module exporting a static factory `F:function(e,t,n){…{initialValue:t,key:e}…}` and a keyed factory `K:function(e,t){let n=W(S,n=>V(e(n),t),{getServerSnapshot:()=>t,onMount(`, each located by shape; key = first arg of every call `(0,A.F)(key,…)` in the modules that require it (a module counts once whatever its number of copies; template, quoted string, own constant or another module's export resolved)
state.persistedAtoms.falsePositiveRisk: calls whose key is built by a non-constant expression (29) are listed in unresolved; keys ending in * are prefixes of runtime-built keys; modules that re-export the factory instead of requiring it are not chased

state.sharedObjects.anchor: none: no `shared-object-*` message, `sharedObjectRepository`, `getSharedObjectSnapshotValue` or `get-shared-object-snapshot` anywhere in the main process or the renderer (the mechanism was removed after 22943)
state.sharedObjects.falsePositiveRisk: `removed` means none of the mechanism's strings exists in any file of either realm; a renamed mechanism would read the same (compare the build's window state sync: bus.toView, state.persistedAtoms)

commands.ids.anchor: command-table assembly `[...tag(A,`webview`),...tag(B,`vscode-only`),...tag(C,`electron-only`)]`; A starts `[{id:`newTask`,titleIntlId:`; id = literal, `Enum.member.id`, or `...[1..9].map(e=>({id:`prefix${e}`}))` expansion
commands.ids.falsePositiveRisk: ids of elements built by other computation are listed in unresolved; vscode-only commands exist only for the VS Code host and never reach the Electron app, kept in byKind so a consumer can drop them

settings.slugs.anchor: `[{slug:`general-settings`},` array in the renderer chunk that holds it (app-initial, app-primary, ...): `slug:` of each element
settings.slugs.falsePositiveRisk: low; the table generates the /settings/<slug> routes. Order is the sidebar order

panel.tabKinds.anchor: two registrar shapes writing one Map, exported by one rspack module and found by what they do: `register(kind,Component,options)` (builds `{...options,<inherited options>,Component,dropDestinations,kind}` and `MAP.set(kind,it)`) and `register({kind,...})` (`MAP.set(meta.kind,meta)`); first arg of every call `(0,A.register)(…)` in the modules that require it (a module counts once whatever its number of copies), resolved from a string, an own constant, another module's export, `D.kind` or a spread descriptor
panel.tabKinds.falsePositiveRisk: tab types whose kind is not statically resolvable (0) are listed in unresolved; builtinTabIdEnum (browser, diff, plan, ...) is the id enum of fixed side-panel tabs, a different thing from registered kinds

items.types.anchor: switches in renderer chunks whose labels include userMessage, agentMessage, commandExecution and contextCompaction; the largest one is the renderer turn-item union
items.types.falsePositiveRisk: the 36-label union mixes protocol ThreadItem types (19) with renderer-synthesised turn items (17: error, steered, todo-list, ...); an item type handled only by `.type===` comparisons and no switch would be missed

apphost.services.anchor: method `createAppHost(e){` -> `return new Host({...})` object literal (+ spreads read by what they evaluate to: `...fn()`, `...(a,{...})`, `...c?{...}:{}`, `...name`, `...a.fn()`; + the host class constructor that drops `getConnection`/`globalState` and adds `browserAuthOperations`)
apphost.services.falsePositiveRisk: a listed key may hold void 0/null in a given window (per-window presence is runtime); conditional keys (platform- or appearance-gated) are marked; services added to the host object after construction would be missed

routes.paths.anchor: JSX Route elements `(0,jsx)(R,{path:...})` in the renderer chunk that holds the route table, R = the dominant component among jsx calls with a path prop; path = template/string literal, const identifier or `${const}` template
routes.paths.falsePositiveRisk: paths built from member expressions or computed (unresolved) and the slug-generated settings routes (see settings.slugs) are not in values; nested route paths are relative to their parent route

i18n.ids.anchor: locale catalogs = renderer chunks named xx-YY-<hash>.js (>400KB) that carry the key "codex.command.newThread":; ids = keys of the default-export object of the largest catalog
i18n.ids.falsePositiveRisk: catalog ids mix content-hash ids (6 chars) and named ids; code defines ~20k more (id,defaultMessage) pairs than the catalogs translate, so "message ids" is 32,385 translated or ~51,800 defined depending on the reading (both reported)

dom.dataAppAttrs.anchor: literal attribute names matching data-app-[a-z0-9-]+ in main-process and renderer JS (css selectors cross-checked)
dom.dataAppAttrs.falsePositiveRisk: names assembled at runtime (data-app-action-${x}) appear only as a literal prefix, if at all; names that occur only in a CSS selector are listed in cssOnly

protocol.schema.falsePositiveRisk: none (generated). Methods only in experimental are gated by the experimentalApi capability

protocol.wireOnly.anchor: literal method names in neither schema, with call-shape evidence: app method->category table (`"thread/start":`thread``), first arg of sendAppServerRequest/sendAppServerExtensionRequest (any shape) and of sendRequest/addNotificationCallback/... (schema namespace only), `methods:[..]` lists, `case`/`.method===` labels (either way round), arrays that also hold a schema method, `x=`ns/name`` assignments next to a `.method` switch (wire-method rewriting); any quote spelling, main-process code in whatever chunks
protocol.wireOnly.falsePositiveRisk: method-shaped strings of other protocols (MCP tools/call, LSP workspace/applyEdit, browser environment/*) share namespaces; only call-shape evidence is counted, bare literals go to weakCandidates. Names built by concatenation are missed. None has a parameter schema

choke.jsx.anchor: `X.Fragment=F,X.jsx=G,X.jsxs=G}` (jsx and jsxs are the same function)
choke.jsx.falsePositiveRisk: a second JSX factory ships inside the in-app browser page-preload bundle (main-process directory); it is a different realm and is not the app renderer

choke.lazy.anchor: none: an rspack renderer loads its lazy modules through the webpack runtime (no Vite preload helper)

choke.react.anchor: `.version=` assignment of the module holding `X.useSyncExternalStore=function` (react) and of the one holding `X.createPortal=function` (react-dom; vendored reconcilers assign no `.version`), each a CJS module of the rspack module map
choke.react.falsePositiveRisk: low; React ships as CJS modules whose version strings are exact. Other bundled copies of react-dom (no .version assignment) are not seen

choke.taps.anchor: the three command sites a tap prepends to: the descriptor array (`X=[{id:`newTask`,`), the default-handler Map (`X=new Map([[`newTask`,`) and the message catalog (`X={...Y,"codex.command.importExternalAgent":`)
choke.taps.falsePositiveRisk: low; the strings are command ids. The locale catalogs hold the message id as data and are not matched by the `X={...Y,` form

choke.menus.anchor: the item builder of a thread's menus, `async function F({scope:S,target:T,actions:A,…,showForkInSidebar:…})` (the sidebar row's and the thread header's menus)
choke.menus.falsePositiveRisk: low; the parameter names are the app's own, and the one other `showForkInSidebar:` is the call site, not a definition

choke.appHost.anchor: `H=C?.createAppHost(e.sender),V=make(port,H);C?.registerAppView(e.sender,V)` in the main-process bundle (the AppHost of each window)
choke.appHost.falsePositiveRisk: none seen; both method names occur only here and in their definitions

ui.exposures.anchor: 80 objects of the app, each located by strings and structure and found exactly once in the renderer chunks (adapters/tools/seams.mjs EXPOSURES; a dry run of the derivers)
ui.exposures.falsePositiveRisk: an exposure whose anchor still matches once but whose object changed meaning is caught by the binding that uses it (canary), not here

lazy.addresses.anchor: static (module id, export) pairs of the lazy imports `Promise.all([A.e(<chunk>),…]).then(A.bind(A,"<id>"))` whose named export the code takes at once (`{X:e}=await …`, `(await …).X`, `.then(e=>e.X)`, `.then(({X:e})=>…)`, `.then(e=>{let{X:t}=e;…})`): what the lazy loads hand to a binding (the id of the module that exports X; a module counts once whatever its number of copies)
lazy.addresses.falsePositiveRisk: pairs only; imports of a whole module (`await …` bound to a name, `.default`) and loads whose export list is built dynamically are not addresses

bindings.sites.anchor: the JSX call sites `jsx)(X,{...})` of the renderer chunks, each binding's prop keys among their props (addresses.json); else object literals carrying them
bindings.sites.falsePositiveRisk: a key set is evidence that the address exists, not of the component's identity (a one-key exact address matches many sites); the canary checks identity at run time
